content.text: Currently, Constants.FEDORA_HOME comes from either the value of the "fedora.home" system property

the FEDORA_HOME environment variable.  Both of these are typically set on a servlet container-wide basis.  Allowing for multiple Fedora homes in one servlet container should be able to use a method (like an init-param in web.xml) that is scoped at the webapp level.

Another challenge to this is the current assumption of the web path "/fedora" in server code.  Where possible, the server code should be changed to not depend on the web path of Fedora.  In instances where it MUST depend on the web path, the value should be taken from a runtime constant.  This constant's value would ideally be determined and set at servlet init() time.
raised priority; this issue is a pain point for Adam@UVA

I believe the system property approach is inappropriate for container-based use (fine for commandline), as a system property can't be set on a per-application basis. Perhaps better use of the existing context configuration would do it; current entries in web.xml alone appear to be insufficient.
javax.servlet.ServletException: Neither the FEDORA_HOME environment variable, nor the fedora.home system property was set
A silly hack to get it mostly working. Doesn't fix the nonsense going on in the FieldSearchServlet, but at least I was able to create objects in both containers.
I'm betting getting data back out might be problematic, but this at least gets it in.

in short, the servercontrollerservlet loads a contextparam with fedora.home in it, then sets the servlet.fedora.home systemproperty, which becomes the first in line in the if/else tree in Context.FedoraHome.getValue(). this should fall through to the default behavior for non-webapp clients, preserving back-woods compatibility.
Thanks McClain!  Applied patch in trunk and updated install guide accordingly.  This now correctly picks up (and prefers) the fedora.home value as specified in web.xml.
It should be possible to deploy multiple instances of Fedora on one server, using one servlet container.

Currently, the most obvious obstacle to this is the fact that Fedora relies on an environment variable to find FEDORA_HOME.  Because of this, in order to have two versions of Fedora on the same server, you must have two servlet containers running as different users, each of which provides its own FEDORA_HOME.
Is there any way to specify FEDORA_HOME in an XML file deployed alongside the WAR file?
